channel.title: AI with Maris — Blog (English)
channel.description: A new article every day about AI in small and mid-sized businesses.

item.title: From Excel chaos to a clean data base: the underrated AI precondition
item.description: AI rarely fails on the AI — usually on the chaos underneath. Why clean data is the most boring and most important step.

item.title: AI in the warehouse and purchasing: three processes that almost always pay off
item.description: Between goods-in and ordering lies a lot of quiet manual work. Three spots where AI eases the load fast.

item.title: Fear of AI in the team: how to bring people along instead of alienating them
item.description: “Is the AI taking my job now?” Ignore that fear and you lose the team — no matter how good the tool is.

item.title: Avoiding lock-in: adopting AI without making yourself dependent
item.description: Today's most convenient AI tool can be tomorrow's expensive trap. How to keep the door open.

item.title: Automation or AI? The difference that decides your budget
item.description: Not every time saving needs AI. Confuse the two and you overpay — or use a sledgehammer to crack a nut.

item.title: AI coaching vs. workshop: why the one-off training barely helps
item.description: A day of workshop, everyone's excited — two weeks later nobody uses it. Why that happens, and what works instead.

item.title: Skilled-worker shortage and AI: no replacement, but a lever
item.description: AI doesn't replace skilled workers — they're far too scarce for that. But it can ease the load on the ones you have. That's where the real value is.

item.title: Agentic AI: from assistant to colleague — the 2026 trend in context
item.description: The buzzword of the year is “agentic”. What's behind it, where it really helps — and why without guardrails the colleague quickly becomes a risk.

item.title: 94 percent without AI: what a current figure reveals about the Mittelstand
item.description: A recent survey says the vast majority of smaller firms don't yet use AI productively. That's not a disgrace — it's an opportunity in plain sight.

item.title: New AI models every six months: which one fits which task?
item.description: Constant new AI models, each stronger than the last. The real skill isn’t knowing the best one — it’s choosing the fitting one.

item.title: The EU AI Act: why the postponed deadlines aren't the all-clear
item.description: The EU has pushed back key AI deadlines. Sounds like a reprieve — but it's no reason to put the topic away again.

item.title: Less scrap, less energy: AI optimisation on the shop floor
item.description: Two cost blocks few people tackle systematically: scrap and energy. Where AI adjusts the levers that escape the eye.

item.title: Securing hands-on knowledge: AI as the memory of your production
item.description: When the colleague with 40 years of experience retires, knowledge leaves with them. AI can help preserve it — before it walks out the door.

item.title: AI in production planning: when the plan reshuffles itself
item.description: A rush order, a sick shift, a broken machine — and the neat plan is waste paper. How AI lets fine planning think along.

item.title: AI in quality control: seeing the defects the eye misses
item.description: By the end of a shift every eye looks tired. How AI vision inspects evenly on the line — and moves the human to where they count.

item.title: Predictive maintenance: foreseeing machine failures before they get expensive
item.description: The most expensive downtime is the one that surprises you. How AI learns to listen to machines — and warns before the line stops.

item.title: Shadow AI in your company: your team already uses ChatGPT — now what?
item.description: While management debates AI strategy, the team already uses ChatGPT. Ban it? Ignore it? Both are risky. There's a third way.

item.title: When an AI pilot is truly worth it
item.description: Whether an AI pilot is any good isn’t decided by the effort but by one question: does it prove a real benefit within a few weeks?

item.title: Starting small isn't thinking small: from the first use case to an AI roadmap
item.description: Starting small isn't giving up the big picture. It's the only route to it that doesn't peter out in the sand.

item.title: AI in accounting: why the paper mountain is the perfect first use case
item.description: People looking to start with AI often hunt for the right project. Usually it's already sitting there: the pile in front of accounting.

item.title: AI in sales: from lead to quote — where automation really saves time
item.description: Good sales runs on contact, not on CRM upkeep. Where AI takes over the grind — and where the human stays irreplaceable.

item.title: What an AI agent with access to your numbers actually gets done
item.description: Not a chatbot that gives tips — an agent that reads your systems and does the work. What Claude Code over MCP takes on in controlling, concretely.

item.title: Why AI only becomes useful once it's allowed into your systems
item.description: An AI chat in the browser doesn't know your business. MCP is the standard that gives it safe access to your real systems — without the tech jargon.

item.title: AI in financial planning: forecasts that are more than rolled-over Excel
item.description: The liquidity plan is outdated the day it's finished. How AI keeps forecasts current continuously and runs scenarios in minutes.

item.title: AI in controlling: the month-end report that explains itself
item.description: The numbers are ready on the 5th, the explanation takes until the 12th. Where AI takes the grind off controlling — without replacing the judgement.

item.title: The AI Workflow for Teachers — teaching materials on autopilot
item.description: A clear AI workflow for teachers takes over typing, formatting and research — without any student data ever entering an AI tool.

item.title: Business-driven AI: when the bottom line steers the project
item.description: Technology-driven means a slick tool nobody needs. Business-driven means every AI pays into a number that matters. Here's how to flip it.

item.title: An early-warning cockpit instead of gut feeling: AI for everyday metrics
item.description: The numbers are already there — no one just sees them in time. How AI turns data into an early-warning system for daily work.

item.title: Prompt basics for your team: what everyone should know
item.description: Not everyone needs to become a prompt expert. But a few ground rules decide whether AI saves time or just creates frustration.

item.title: Five questions to judge any AI use case in ten minutes
item.description: Not every idea makes a good first AI case. Five questions let you sort, in ten minutes, what is worth it — and what to skip.
